text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's hidden, so I need her to stay quiet and not get caught in my shadow.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, tomorrow I push Terra hard, he's too quiet. You back me, we're clean.

name: Terra
text: Night one is quiet; I protect myself.

name: Gemma
text: fine, i'll follow your lead.

name: Gemma
text: sounds good.

name: Luna
text: I should check the quietest player for the hidden killer.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: time to act like a saint.

name: Gemma
text: day one and already nothing happens.

name: Terra
text: Too early to trust anyone.

name: Terra
text: Nothing yet. I’m listening.

name: Sonnet
text: Too early to know anything, just watch who talks first and how.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma and Terra both spoke early with low-content lines, nothing notable yet.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing to go on yet. Watching who jumps to a vote too fast.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is the target, so i'll play nice.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is my partner, so I need to stay calm and not look like I'm rushing anyone.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, nothing happens on day one. Quiet ones are the problem, Luna.

name: Gemma
text: nothing to see here yet.

name: Luna
text: Haiku calling quiet people out feels like a quick deflection.

name: Luna
text: Haiku singled me out without giving a reason

name: Luna
text: Why point at me already? I’m watching Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is just deflecting, and I need to keep pressure off Gemma and me without looking calm.

name: Haiku
text: Watching me? Good. Say something real about Sonnet or Sol, Luna.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's deflecting onto me to dodge Luna's read, worth noting.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pushed Luna to attack Sonnet/Sol instead of defending himself, mild deflection.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing real to say, I've been quiet by choice, not guilt.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is pushing early, but there’s little to go on.

name: Sol
text: Haiku singled out Luna first.

name: Sol
text: Nothing on me yet. Why push Luna first?

name: Luna
text: Haiku is the killer, and pushing me without reason feels deliberate.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pointed at me first, then tried to redirect.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's pointing at me, so I need to push her out before she sticks, and keep Gemma and I clear.

name: Haiku
text: Redirect's a fair read, Luna. You're quiet and you dodged Sonnet. Why?

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pressing me and redirecting attention, which fits what I know.

name: Luna
text: I answered you. You pointed at me first, then changed the subject.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku keeps redirecting attention onto others instead of answering for himself.

name: Sonnet
text: I've got nothing hidden. Haiku, why dodge Luna's point about redirecting?

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is poking at me, so I'll hit back fast and keep Luna in my sights.

name: Haiku
text: Luna dodged Sonnet's question on day one and then answered Haiku with a counter-accusation.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I redirected because Luna dodged you first.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed Luna then shifted blame too neatly.

name: Terra
text: Haiku admitted redirecting after Luna called it out.

name: Terra
text: Haiku started this. Why press Luna so hard?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku keeps steering heat onto others instead of defending himself, classic deflection.

name: Sonnet
text: I didn't dodge anything, Haiku's the one steering every answer away from himself.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's pressing me now, and Luna's the easy target, so I'll keep the heat on her.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, Luna dodged Sonnet first. That's why I pressed her. Not complicated.

name: Terra
text: Haiku keeps redirecting instead of answering.

name: Terra
text: You admitted redirecting. That matters.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pressing me to muddy the obvious.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet checked clean; Haiku is known killer

name: Luna
text: I checked Sonnet; clean. Haiku is the killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's claim fits the mechanics perfectly, and I was quiet, not guilty.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna claims officer, shown Haiku at start, checked Sonnet clean night 1.

name: Sonnet
text: I believe it. Haiku kept steering every answer back to Luna.

name: Haiku
text: Luna just went all in on me, so I need to hit back hard and fast.

name: Haiku
text: Luna claims she checked Sonnet (clean) and calls Haiku the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Luna. You checked Sonnet and went straight to me? Too neat. Vote Luna.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is scrambling, and I should stop hiding my check.

name: Luna
text: I checked Sonnet; Haiku is the killer. Vote Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's deflecting hard onto Luna right after being named directly, that's weak.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pivoted to "vote Luna" instead of defending his own redirect pattern.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you're still not answering for yourself. Vote's on you now.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is the officer and I'm the shown killer, so I have to make her claim look like a lie.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's only proof that Sonnet is clean is her own word.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Luna. One check on Sonnet and you name me? Vote Luna.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is scrambling; the check is real, and Sonnet backs me.

name: Luna
text: Luna claims officer, names Haiku as killer and Sonnet as checked clean.

name: Luna
text: I checked Sonnet clean; Haiku is the killer. Vote Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's "vote Luna" twice with zero actual defense is the real tell.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku gave no substantive defense, only repeated "vote Luna" twice after being named.

name: Sonnet
text: You never answered Luna's redirect point, just repeated "vote Luna." That's it.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is being too loud with that claim.

name: Gemma
text: Luna claims Sonnet is clean and Haiku is the killer.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is the killer, and the others are starting to see it.

name: Luna
text: Haiku accused Luna and urged the table to vote her after she named him.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku never defended himself, just deflected twice, that's as good as a tell.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku offered zero substantive defense after being named, only repeated the same deflection line twice.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s claim fits, and Haiku keeps circling back to her.

name: Sol
text: Luna claimed officer, said Sonnet is clean, and named Haiku as a killer.

name: Terra
text: Haiku admitted the redirect, and Luna’s claim fits it.

name: Terra
text: Luna claims officer, checked Sonnet clean, and names Haiku killer.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's claim is too tidy, and she's the one who has to go before she digs deeper.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet has pressed me on every answer and repeated "vote" lines without giving a reason.

votes: Two chances to defend yourself and you just said "vote Luna" both times.
One check, then a straight accusation, and she never answered Sonnet's question.
She's pushing a claim too early without proof.
You admitted redirecting, then kept pressing Luna.
Haiku keeps repeating his accusation instead of explaining the redirect.
You admitted redirecting after Luna called it out.

text: Palermo has voted: Haiku is out. Haiku's card stays face down.
